hangulquest.story.house_first.title: My first house
hangulquest.story.house_first.p1: It is morning. I am in the forest. Today I build a house.
hangulquest.story.house_first.p2: First I chop down trees. There are lots of logs. I make planks.
hangulquest.story.house_first.p3: There is stone next to the forest. And I mine the stone.
hangulquest.story.house_first.p4: Now I build the house. I put a door in the house. I put in glass, too.
hangulquest.story.house_first.p5: Inside the house I place a bed. I place a chest, too. Last, I place a torch.
hangulquest.story.house_first.p6: The house is warm. I lie down on the bed. Now I sleep. It is really good!
hangulquest.story.fire_night.title: The first night
hangulquest.story.fire_night.p1: The sun sets. Night comes. It is dark outside.
hangulquest.story.fire_night.p2: I am in front of the house. There is a moon in the sky. There are stars, too.
hangulquest.story.fire_night.p3: I am scared! But I have a torch.
hangulquest.story.fire_night.p4: I place the torch. The fire is bright. Now I am not scared.
hangulquest.story.fire_night.p5: I sit down next to the torch. The firelight is warm. The moon is pretty, too.
hangulquest.story.fire_night.p6: The night is long. But it is okay. I have a torch.
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.title: The small field
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.p1: I am in the field. Today I plant wheat seeds.
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.p2: First I take the hoe and dig the soil. I plant the seeds and give them water.
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.p3: It rains at night. In the morning the wheat grows.
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.p4: The wheat is yellow. Now I harvest the wheat.
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.p5: I make bread from the wheat. The bread is really tasty!
hangulquest.story.field_harvest.p6: I give wheat to the cow, too. And the cow gives me milk. I am happy.
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.title: The animals at our house
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.p1: There is a fence next to our house. There are many animals inside the fence.
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.p2: There is one cow, three chickens and two sheep.
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.p3: In the morning the chickens lay eggs. I collect the eggs.
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.p4: There is one pig, too. The pig eats carrots.
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.p5: There is a cat, too. The cat sleeps inside the house.
hangulquest.story.animals_farm.p6: I am here with the animals. I am really happy!
hangulquest.culture.ondol.title: Ondol: heated floors
hangulquest.culture.ondol.summary: In an ondol room the floor is warm. The heat of the fire goes under the floor.
hangulquest.culture.ondol.text: Ondol is the traditional Korean floor heating. A wood fire burns in a stove opening next to the room, and the hot air and smoke flow through channels under a stone floor covered with clay and paper before they leave through a chimney. In the game, the furnace is the closest thing to that fire.
hangulquest.culture.hanok.title: Hanok: the traditional house
hangulquest.culture.hanok.summary: A hanok is built from wood and roof tiles. The ends of the roof curve up to the sky.
hangulquest.culture.hanok.text: A hanok is a traditional Korean house with a wooden frame, clay walls and a roof of curved clay tiles called giwa. The wide eaves give shade in summer and let the low winter sun reach the room. In the game, deepslate tiles make a good gray giwa roof.
hangulquest.culture.jangdok.title: Jangdok: jars for sauces
hangulquest.culture.jangdok.summary: Inside the jangdok there are soybean paste and soy sauce.
hangulquest.culture.jangdok.text: A jangdok is a large earthenware jar in which soy sauce, soybean paste (doenjang) and chili paste (gochujang) ferment and are kept. The clay lets air through, and the jars stand in the sun on a raised platform in the yard called jangdokdae. The barrel is the closest storage block in the game.
hangulquest.culture.hanbok.title: Hanbok: traditional clothes
hangulquest.culture.hanbok.summary: Hanbok has beautiful colors. The colors come from flowers and plants.
hangulquest.culture.hanbok.text: Hanbok is traditional Korean clothing with a short jacket, the jeogori, and a wide skirt or trousers. Its colors used to come from plants: safflower for red, indigo for blue and gardenia for yellow. In the game, flowers give dyes in much the same way.
hangulquest.culture.kimchi.title: Kimchi
hangulquest.culture.kimchi.summary: Kimchi is made from napa cabbage. You add salt and chili powder.
hangulquest.culture.kimchi.text: Kimchi is a Korean side dish of salted vegetables, usually napa cabbage, mixed with chili powder, garlic and ginger and left to ferment. Families traditionally make enough for the winter together in late autumn; this custom, called kimjang, was added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage in 2013. The game has no kimchi, but the fermented spider eye is a fermented ingredient, too.
hangulquest.culture.seollal.title: Seollal: Lunar New Year
hangulquest.culture.seollal.summary: At Seollal the family gathers. They eat tteokguk (rice cake soup).
hangulquest.culture.seollal.text: Seollal is the Korean Lunar New Year, on the first day of the first lunar month, in late January or February. Families gather, the young bow deeply to their elders (sebae), and everybody eats tteokguk, rice cake soup, to begin the new year. The date moves every year because it follows the lunar calendar.
hangulquest.culture.chuseok.title: Chuseok: the harvest festival
hangulquest.culture.chuseok.summary: At Chuseok the full moon rises. They eat songpyeon (rice cakes).
hangulquest.culture.chuseok.text: Chuseok is the Korean harvest festival, on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month, when the autumn moon is full. Families travel to their hometowns, honor their ancestors, and share songpyeon, half-moon-shaped rice cakes filled with sesame, chestnuts or sweet beans. Like Seollal, it is a three-day holiday around the date.
hangulquest.culture.yutnori.title: Yutnori: the game with sticks
hangulquest.culture.yutnori.summary: In yutnori you throw four yut sticks. Do, gae, geol, yut or mo comes up.
hangulquest.culture.yutnori.text: Yutnori is a traditional board game, often played at Seollal. You throw four wooden sticks and count how many land flat side up: one is do, two is gae, three is geol, four is yut and none is mo. The five names are said to mean pig, dog, sheep, cow and horse; in the game, two planks make exactly four sticks.

hangulquest.ui.research.consent:
Hangul Quest research export

You made this zip yourself, on your computer, with the button "Export research data" in the journal settings. Nothing was sent anywhere. Whether you share it is entirely up to you; if you do not want to, just delete it.

What is in it
- reviews.ndjson: one line per answer or encounter with a word: the time, a hashed word id, how it was answered (mode and grade), how long it took, how many days passed since the previous review, a short place label (quiz, quest, card or probe), the experiment arm of the word, and whether it is a core word.
- The word ids are hashed with a random key that was made for this export and then thrown away. The same word has a different hash in every export, so the ids cannot be turned back into words and two exports cannot be linked.

What is not in it
No player, account, world, server or chat names, no coordinates, no IP address, no settings, no quest or trail names. The times are real: they show when you played.

Why share it
The Hangul Quest project compares review settings word by word to learn what helps people remember Korean. Sharing is voluntary and manual: attach the file yourself, where the project page says to.
hangulquest.ui.research.placement.title: Vocabulary check
hangulquest.ui.research.placement.intro: About 3 minutes. Korean words appear one at a time. Press Yes if you know what the word means, No if you do not. Some words are made up: saying Yes to those lowers your score. It is optional, and you can stop at any time.
hangulquest.ui.research.placement.skip: Esc stops the check; nothing is saved.
hangulquest.ui.research.placement.score: Score %s of 100. You knew %s of %s real words and claimed %s of %s made-up words.
hangulquest.ui.research.placement.seeded: %s words you know will come back in a few days for a quick check.
hangulquest.ui.research.placement.unreli: You said Yes to many made-up words, so no words were added.
